climate_pressure: Coastal land and infrastructure risks, including projected sea-level rise.
documented_impact: The national plan proposes higher-ground development and relocation of coastal assets.
fcv_mediator: Legacy wartime explosives, mined-land pinnacles and rehabilitation costs limit usable higher-ground land.
possible_consequence: Land rehabilitation for housing, water catchment and infrastructure is constrained, complicating the planned adaptation pathway.
institutions: Government of the Republic of Nauru
alternative_explanations: Phosphate-mining damage, outdated land legislation, finance and technical capacity are additional constraints; the explosives' separate contribution is not quantified.
uncertainty: Historical war legacy, not current armed conflict. No explosive inventory, clearance cost, site hazard boundary or measured relocation delay is established.
resilience_factors: The Higher Ground Initiative and land-use planning offer an adaptation framework; financing and delivery remain conditional.
compact_statement: Wartime explosive remnants and mined-land rehabilitation costs constrain the usable higher-ground land needed for planned coastal adaptation.
